description: Slowing of gait speed, loss of smell and increased depression, anxiety and stress have been associated with lower cognitive performance among older adults. The Minnesota Memory Project is a longitudinal study of community-dwelling adults 55 and older that investigates lifestyle factors associated with cognitive aging.

title: A QUALITATIVE STUDY OF ADULT PROTECTIVE SERVICES PRACTITIONERS RESPONDING TO CASES OF ELDER ABUSE AND SELF-NEGLECT
creator: Andie MacNeil, Erin Salvo, David Burnes
description: Adult Protective Services (APS) practitioners play a critical role in supporting older adults experiencing elder abuse and self-neglect (EASN), however, very little research has examined their experiences, from their perspectives. The purpose of this study was to examine the experiences of APS practitioners responding to allegations of EASN.

title: INFLUENZA VACCINATION AND OLFACTION IN OLDER ADULTS: FINDINGS FROM HEALTH ABC
creator: Yaqun Yuan, Keran Chamberlin, Chenxi Li, Zhehui Luo, Teresa Tian, Eleanor Simonsick, Honglei Chen
description: Olfactory impairment is common in older adults and is likely associated with multiple adverse health outcomes. However, few risk or protective factors for olfactory impairment in older adults have been identified. We examined the cross-sectional association between flu vaccination and olfaction among 2507 participants of the Health, Aging and Body Composition study (aged 71-82 years, 51.7% women, and 37.4% Blacks).

title: ANALYZING THE INFLUENCE OF MIDLIFE EMPLOYMENT TRAJECTORIES ON COGNITIVE AGING IN CHILE
creator: Magdalena Delaporte, Jere Behrman
description: As the global population ages, understanding the factors contributing to healthy aging becomes increasingly crucial. This paper delves into the relationship between mid-life employment trajectories and later-life cognition, utilizing a Chilean longitudinal dataset. Employing the Group-Based Trajectory Model (GBTM), distinct employment trajectories for males and females between 1980 and 2016 are estimated.

title: BURDEN AMONG INFORMAL CAREGIVERS OF OLDER ADULTS IN GHANA: A SCOPING REVIEW
creator: Joana Okine, Nicole Ruggiano
description: The aging population in Ghana has experienced a significant increase, expanding tenfold from 213,477 in 1960 to 1,991,736 in 2021 during the last population census. Projections indicate that by 2030, the population of persons aged 60 and above will hit 2.8 million (Mba, 2010).

title: DOES PSYCHOLOGICAL FLEXIBILITY MEDIATE CARE-RELATED STRESS ON QUALITY OF LIFE FOR DEMENTIA CAREGIVERS?
creator: Elizabeth Fauth, Ty Aller, Jacob Gossner, Audrey Juhasz, Michael Levin
description: Caregivers of individuals with dementia experience care-related burden and stressful reactions to behavioral and psychological symptoms of dementia (BPSD) which can negatively impact multiple domains of life, including decreased global quality of life (QoL). Transdiagnostic interventions, such as those using Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) benefit dementia caregivers by addressing underlying mechanisms that impact depression, anxiety, QoL, and more.

title: PROMOTING GERONTOLOGICAL TRAINING AND POSITIVE ATTITUDES OF AGING THROUGH HIGH-IMPACT TEACHING PRACTICES
creator: Aimee Fox, Bethany Riding
description: Despite being the youngest state, Utah, along with the rest of the United States, has a growing aging population. There is demand from state leaders and employers for individuals, families, and a workforce that are knowledgeable about the experiences and needs of older adults.

title: ASSOCIATION BETWEEN SELF-REALIZATION AND HEALTH OUTCOMES IN FAMILY CAREGIVING DYADS
creator: Cristina de Rosa, Weijun Wang, Yu-Ping Chang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Self-realization, such as perceptions of life having meaning and purpose, can potentially influence health in older adults and their family caregivers, but how dyad members may contribute to each other’s outcomes is less well understood. This analysis examined whether self-realization in older adults and their family caregivers was associated with their own, and each other’s, mental health and perceived general health.

title: SANDWICH GENERATION CAREGIVING: NEGATIVE RELATIONSHIP QUALITY AND BURNOUT
creator: Sabine Lohmar, Erika Fenstermacher, Montgomery Owsiany, Catherine Ju, Barry Edelstein
description: The sandwich generation provides caregiving for both their children and their aging parents. These caregivers often experience low satisfaction, depression, and burnout, yet little is known about their contributing factors. For example, researchers have not investigated the role of relationship quality among sandwich generation caregivers, who face unique challenges.

title: CONNECTIONS: INTERGENERATIONAL DIGITAL STORYTELLING FOR CULTIVATING RESILIENCE ACROSS LIFESPAN
creator: Vera Ansie, Crispin Mbamba
description: This innovative study used intergenerational digital storytelling to explore resilience and fortitude across cultures. It aimed to develop and evaluate a culturally grounded intervention for synergistically cultivating resilience among older adults and youth through shared narratives and strengthened intergenerational ties. The participatory methods engaged older adult-youth dyads in one U.S.

title: BEYOND BORDERS: LONG-DISTANCE CAREGIVING AND SLEEP HABITS IN SOUTH ASIAN COMMUNITIES
creator: Aziza Siddiqui, Srujana Chekuri, Akankshya Chataut, Dinesh Karki, Julie Blaskewicz Boron
description: Caregiving is generally altruistic in South Asian (SA) communities; however, caregiving activities can still create significant strain for caregivers depending on situational factors, including sleep and built environments (Hossain et al., 2020). Particularly, long-distance caregivers may grapple with the added complexities of not being physically present to provide care.

title: FEAR OF FALLING INTERACTS WITH ACTN3 GENOTYPE TO PREDICT FAST GAIT SPEED IN OLDER ADULTS
creator: Allon Goldberg, Summer Burkhardt, Hayden Norris, Johnathon Garber, Natalie Little, Jaiden Kendall, Joseph Sucic
description: Deficits in walking speed are associated with poor health outcomes in older adults. The alpha-actinin-3 gene (ACTN3) harbors the R577X polymorphism, which influences muscle function and physical performance in older adults. Fear of falling (FOF) is associated with gait, mobility and physical performance deficits in older adults.

title: ATTITUDES TOWARD MOTIVATIONAL MESSAGING IN A DIGITAL HEALTH ACTIVITY PROGRAM FOR OLDER FAMILY CARE PARTNERS
creator: Dawon Baik, Paul Cook, Catherine Jankowski
description: Older family care partners of patients with heart failure (HF-FCPs) often experience physical, psychological, and social health issues due to age-related health needs, less emotional support, and social isolation. We developed a tailored digital health physical activity (PA) program, TPA4You that includes videoconferencing with a health coach, wearable sensor, and motivational messaging.

title: A CROSS-CULTURAL ANALYSIS OF PREFERENCES AND ATTITUDES TOWARD ADVANCED DIRECTIVES IN TAIWAN AND THAILAND
creator: Hui-Ching Weng, Duan-Rung Chen, Krungkraipetch Kiiti, Inchai Puangtong
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). IntroductionAdvance directives (ADs) are pivotal in healthcare planning, indicating preferences for medical treatment in critical conditions. This study examines ADs attitudes and experiences between Taiwan and Thailand, highlighting cultural influences on end-of-life care. MethodEmploying pairing matching, the study selected 259 matched pairs from an initial Taiwanese pool of 1488 and a Thai sample of 268 based on gender, age, education, and medical work background.

title: AD-RISK FACTORS AND TIMED UP AND GO TASKS IN IMPAIRED AND UNIMPAIRED OLDER ADULTS
creator: Ashley Price, Megan Stradtman, Jessica Alber, Maeve Durkin
description: The Timed Up and Go (TUG) is a clinical assessment tool evaluating mobility and dual-task function. This study examined TUG performance in a sample of cognitively unimpaired (CU) older adults at low risk (LR)/high risk (HR) for Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and a group of mild cognitive impairment (MCI) patients.

title: NURSING HOME STAFF CARE APPROACHES ARE ASSOCIATED WITH MEALTIME DIFFICULTIES IN OLDER ADULTS WITH DEMENTIA
creator: Kyuri Lee, Heather Suh, Wen Liu
description: Nonverbal mealtime care is critical for optimizing eating performance and mealtime behaviors of residents with dementia (RwD), especially for those with limited verbal communication abilities. Understanding the relationship between care staff’s nonverbal approaches and RwD’s mealtime behaviors help guide the development of evidence-based, effective mealtime interventions.

title: AGING AMONG JAPANESE OVERSEAS/EXPATRIATES: A COMPREHENSIVE MIXED METHODS STUDY
creator: Itsuko Toyama
description: The challenges of aging for Japanese individuals living abroad have received limited attention in both Japan and their countries of residence, and they are underrepresented in academic research. This marginalization derives from the small population of Japanese expatriates and the ambiguity surrounding the term “Japanese,” as a nationality and cultural identity.

title: DIFFERENCES IN SELF-CARE AND QUALITY OF LIFE BETWEEN SPOUSES AND ADULT CHILDREN IN PATIENTS WITH PARKINSON’S DISEASE
creator: Juhee Lee, Eunyoung Kim, Hyeran Park, Kiyeon Kim
description: Self-care of patients with chronic illness involves various caregiver types like spouses, adult children, and other relatives or friends. Several studies have reported differences in self-care and quality of life (QOL) according to caregiver type in patients with chronic illness. Nevertheless, there are few studies comparing the difference by caregiver type in patients with Parkinson’s disease (PD).

title: THE INNER DYNAMICS OF THE OLD AND SOCIALLY WITHDRAWN IN JAPAN: INSIGHTS FOR INTERVENTIONS FROM CASE STUDY ANALYSES
creator: Tomoko Ikeuchi, Cullen Hayashida
description: An increasing number of older adults in Japan are refusing social support even when offered. This lack of support elevates their risk of health deterioration, delays evacuation in disaster scenarios, and increases the likelihood of premature and lonely deaths with inadequate closures.

title: RECRUITMENT STRATEGIES IN LONG-TERM CARE: NEW AND NOVEL APPROACHES
creator: Cathy Maxwell, Judith Tate, Lisa Juckett, Kelley Colopietro, Abbey Kilpatrick, Lorraine Mion, Nilanjan Sarkar
description: Older adults residing in long term care (LTC) can benefit from social and behavioral research to improve health outcomes and promote evidence-based practice; however, recruitment is often difficult and time/cost-intensive. Systematic reviews of literature report recruitment barriers, as well as specific recruitment strategies.

title: AN INVESTIGATION OF CDSMP OUTCOMES FOR PARTICIPANTS ENROLLING WITH DIFFERENT LEVELS OF NEED
creator: Abby Teply, Christine McKibbin, Joshua Clapp, Stacy Carling, Laurance Goodwin, Catherine Carrico, Barbara Dabrowski, Elizabeth Punke

title: ASSOCIATION AND INTERACTION BETWEEN RESILIENCE AND PSYCHOLOGICAL DISTRESS IN DISABLED ELDERLY–CAREGIVER DYADS
creator: Anni Wang
description: ObjectivesThe aim of this study was to explore the interaction between resilience and psychological distress in disabled elderly-caregiver. title: CULTURAL DIFFERENCES IN MEDICATION BURDEN OF OLDER HOSPITALIZED PATIENTS IN MEDICAL UNITS
creator: Juliana Smichenko, Ksenya Shulyaev, Efrat Shadmi, Nosaiba Rayan-Gharra, Nurit Gur-Yaish, Anna Zisberg

title: CLINICAL EFFICACY OF A DIGITAL COGNITIVE ASSESSMENTS IN DETECTING COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENTS: A POOLED ANALYSIS

creator: Shinae Choi, Maria Pisu
